analysis: The exact rationale treats a performed one-time command as necessarily operative until revocation because the order has no express termination-on-performance wording. The current pinned owner ruling instead requires separating a command exhausted by established use/performance from surviving consequences. DOI testimony supplies affirmative interim-submission evidence, rather than merely a missed or elapsed deadline. That makes the categorical premise inadequate to sustain this first-end conclusion. Receipt, routing and completeness limitations prevent adopting the testimony date, the 45-day deadline, or any invented date as the exact first end; they do not erase the evidence that interim submission occurred.
applicability: EO13792 sec2(d) independently requires an interim report to the President through four specified executive officials within 45 days, covering Bears Ears and any other designations selected by the Secretary, with recommendations. DOI testimony identifies a submitted Interim Report specifically addressing Bears Ears, making actual performance relevant to this exact one-time command.
